location_qualifier: Lunga / Guadalcanal, with the 132nd RCT less 1st Battalion
source_locator: R2225: ch. IX, p. 213; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9
notes: The 132nd RCT (less the 1st Battalion) landed on 8 December 1942 (Miller, ch. IX). Miller, ch. X, later places the 2nd Battalion in the Lunga perimeter during the December Mount Austen attack, which is consistent with an 8 December landing with the RCT. Confidence 0.7, matching C12814.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X; R2226: ch. IX, 2 January assault on Hill 27
current_activity: capturing Hill 27 and holding it against Japanese counterattacks
notes: Miller, ch. X, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that on 2 January 1943 the 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, completed the envelopment and took Hill 27 (Zimmerman: from the rear, tying in with the 1st and 3rd Battalions). Commander Lt. Col. George F. Ferry (Miller). Confidence 0.7: two official families. Matches the promoted regiment claim C12915.

current_activity: landing the reinforced battalion unopposed at Verahue
notes: Miller, ch. XV: the reinforced 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, landed unopposed at Verahue on 1 February 1943. Matches regiment claim C12918. Commander Lt. Col. George F. Ferry. Confidence 0.5: one official family.

current_activity: advancing from Marovovo to Kamimbo Bay
notes: Miller, ch. XV: on 8 February Colonel Ferry's force advanced from Marovovo to Kamimbo Bay after finding abandoned landing craft. Matches regiment claim C12919. Confidence 0.5: one official family.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV; R2226: ch. IX
notes: Miller, ch. XV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that between 1600 and 1700 on 9 February the 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, marched into Tenaro and met the 1st Battalion, 161st Infantry, ending organised fighting. Commander Lt. Col. George F. Ferry (Miller). Confidence 0.7. Matches C12920.
